attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, giving his own expectation.

semantics.note: 'I do not expect' is an unqualified expectation, so it is a scored forecast. 'Perhaps I'll be proven wrong' admits he could be wrong; it does not turn the prediction into a stated probability. No deadline is given. The proposition keeps his wording and the qualifier.

contract.note: Reading 'very much' as no substantial case-specific enforcement (charges, penalties, binding restrictions) is a fair, ordinary reading. Under the early-resolution rule, only contradiction can come early; support needs a fuller record.

evidence.note: Reports a DOJ criminal inquiry already under way before the post was published. It is not a qualifying post-publication enforcement action.
Dated on the evaluation date. It reports an ongoing investigation and no charges. That is not a conclusive event either way.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. Only one day had passed by the evaluation date. The packet shows a pre-existing DOJ inquiry and no charges, entity listing or penalties after publication, so no conclusive event contradicts the forecast. A short stretch without action cannot support it either. The outcome stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own essay.

semantics.note: The firm causal claim is kept: forced early GPU purchases led to higher RAM and consumer-electronics prices, done for NVIDIA's growth. The moral judgments are rightly left out.

contract.note: The plain readings (at least $2B, at least two months, a broad market price effect, coercion beyond simply unused inventory) are ordinary and fair. The claim needs attribution evidence that the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: TrendForce links tight memory supply to suppliers shifting capacity toward AI and server products. It does not show NVIDIA compelled any purchases or isolate their effect.
Notebook cost pressure from memory and CPUs. The retail figures are modelled scenarios, and nothing ties them to premature NVIDIA deliveries.
Says the forced-stockpiling allegation is unverified. That is a gap in the evidence, not affirmative disproof.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows broad AI-driven memory price pressure plus other factors such as CPU costs. Nothing establishes that NVIDIA compelled premature hyperscaler purchases, that such purchases caused the price rises, or the claimed motive. Nothing affirmatively refutes the claim either, so it is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own inference in his own essay.

semantics.note: A compound historical claim. 'It appears' is kept as a qualifier, and 'clearly in violation' is stated firmly. The proposition covers knowledge, interference, motive and violation.

contract.note: Assessing the compound inference as a whole, and requiring corroborated evidence for each part, is a fair ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Secondary account of NYT reporting that NVIDIA's general counsel contacted BIS agents during the probe. It supports only the narrow contact element, not knowledge, intent or a violation.
Reproduced NYT report: the case moved to DOJ to avoid compromise, and a criminal inquiry continues. That limits the 'block' claim but does not settle it.
NVIDIA says it put Megaspeed on its internal block list in June 2025. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: Reporting confirms only that NVIDIA's counsel contacted Commerce investigators before Commerce paused its probe. Nothing establishes that NVIDIA knew of the affair, intended to obstruct, acted to preserve sales, or that actual export violations occurred. The counter-points (a continuing DOJ inquiry, NVIDIA's self-reported block) do not refute the claim. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. The Benzinga quote is his supporting material.

semantics.note: The proposition adds 'misleading' and softens 'wasn't possible' to 'inconsistent'. The exact sentence asserts that NVIDIA made the claim and that the claim was financially impossible. The contract flags this and scores the exact elements.

contract.note: The result depends on whether 'chips' means packages or dies, and on a revenue reconciliation the speaker did not give. Requiring a proper reconciliation is fair.

evidence.note: A third-party keynote transcript has Huang saying six million Blackwells had shipped. This supports the 'company claimed' element only.
Reports that a slide footnote counted 6M dies, about 3M packages. The revenue objection comes from a social-media thread, not a verified reconciliation.

reviews.rationale: NVIDIA's six-million statement is documented. The core claim, that revenue comparison made the shipments impossible, has no reconciliation of realized prices, timing and recognized revenue in the packet. The dies-versus-packages clarification neither proves nor refutes impossibility. Unresolved.
